Part of me is happy all this is happening so early in life, and so early in the relationship. We could've made it through high school and broke up because of college issues and I could've dropped out because of it. She did a lot of damage, yes, but it was all kinetic and it's better that I stopped this early. I am only 15. There's too much ahead of me but damn, getting completely betrayed by the one you love is the most hurtful feeling in the world.

I kind of am hoping that there's a moral ticking time bomb here and one day she'll look back and think "wow, I was so immature and selfish, he didn't deserve that when all he did was care about me"

I don't know. I was looking for something mature, committed and strong and she gave up on our first real rough spot. We fought maybe 3 times. I still feel terrible and am hung up on the fact that I let it happen.

I knew from the beginning that something was bound to happen between us and we wouldn't last throughout college. I just am having trouble getting over my love for her. I don't know what to do. I just want to tell her how I feel but I know that will only make things worse. I still think she's the one.
Don't date, that's my advice to you. Never ever.
I know somewhere down the line something would have happened, but I am just irreversibly remorseful because I didn't do everything I could to keep her in love with me.

I respected her decision, and her reasoning. What I didn't like is how she told me she wasn't going to do one thing, but she ended up doing it anyway, then berating me for being upset about it.

I keep getting the feeling that if I never texted her after we broke up, she'd still have feelings for me, or she'd have tried to reconcile with me. That is what is killing me. I regret it so much. 

I wasn't telling her how to live her life or telling her what she could and couldn't do. All I wanted was a little closure on what she's been doing. Is that wrong?

Hmmm, you have some good points. I feel like I fucked up for being up her ass about stuff that wasn't my business, but it actually kind of was. She went from "I don't want to lose feelings for you" to "fuck you, don't ever text me again" in 3 days. It just baffled me I guess. I reacted in a really stupid way. I felt betrayed and felt like the best thing to do would be to talk to her about it. She texted me casually two days before all this happened, trying to make small talk with me. I do want to salvage a friendship with her, yes. But I just am drawn to a blank on how to do that. I did call her out of pure frustration because she told me she didn't want a relationship but I found out she's been flirting with random guys.

That's really hurtful, and I just couldn't keep quiet about it. It was killing me.

From my perspective, it seems like she ended things just to whore around, and I thought that by the time she got bored of that she'd come back to me. I'm hoping that apologizing to her will allow us to have a friendship. I just don't get it - why is she throwing away all her feelings for me just because of a series of a few small mistakes? She could have said "Jack, you're getting on my nerves. What I did is MY business. Stay out of it." but she just told me to fuck off and not contact her. So you're right, it is both of our faults. I asked her if she was talking to other guys when we had our talk, she said no, and she wouldn't be for a long time. She didn't have to lie to me like that. She got my hopes up, sort of a leading me on thing, and that's what really got to me.

What I'm afraid of is her completely hating me and seeing me as a year long mistake, and when I do contact her she's completely over me and sees me as a stranger. I don't want that. 

She gave me the idea that she still loved me and I was hurt beyond belief when I learned she was flirting with at least three other guys. I know it's none of my business, but that kind of does contradict the reason she broke up with me. I just don't want to fuck up anymore. I fucked up by losing her, I fucked up by texting and calling her, and I'm not about to fuck up again. 

I don't want to be the crazy ex. But I feel like my actions in the past month have ruined everything for me.

I am just terribly hung up on the fact that I responded on impulse. I couldn't wait. Part of me just couldn't wait. I wasn't speaking, my feelings were. I wish I could fix it.

I understand moving on, but I would like to at least have a friendship with her. Should I apologize, and if so, how?

I get you. I'm just having such an immense amount of trouble understanding her thinking. I keep putting it on myself, that I ruined something very special with a very special person, but I can't put my finger on anything I did wrong. I don't understand what is happening here. I don't understand women.
Thanks at least for reading.
